has-bled.title: HAS-BLED score

items.label: Abnormal renal function (dialysis, renal transplantation, or serum creatinine ≥200 μmol/L)
Abnormal liver function (chronic hepatic disease, or bilirubin >2× ULN with AST/ALT/ALP >3× ULN)
Drugs — concomitant antiplatelet agents or NSAIDs

has-bled.interpretation: Derived in a 2010 atrial-fibrillation cohort to estimate 1-year major-bleeding risk. Current ESC guidance cautions against using a bleeding-risk score alone to decide whether to start, continue or withhold anticoagulation.

source.text: Pisters R, Lane DA, Nieuwlaat R, de Vos CB, Crijns HJGM, Lip GYH. A novel user-friendly score (HAS-BLED) to assess 1-year risk of major bleeding in patients with atrial fibrillation: the Euro Heart Survey. Chest. 2010;138(5):1093-1100.

cha2ds2-vasc.title: CHA₂DS₂-VASc score

items.label: Congestive heart failure or left ventricular dysfunction
Vascular disease (prior myocardial infarction, peripheral artery disease, or aortic plaque)

cha2ds2-vasc.interpretation: Derived in a 2009/2010 atrial-fibrillation cohort to stratify thromboembolic risk; a given total can reflect different underlying risk depending on which components contribute to it. The 2024 ESC guideline uses a sex-excluded variant (CHA₂DS₂-VA, max 8) instead of this original formulation.

source.text: Lip GYH, Nieuwlaat R, Pisters R, Lane DA, Crijns HJGM. Refining clinical risk stratification for predicting stroke and thromboembolism in atrial fibrillation using a novel risk factor-based approach: the Euro Heart Survey on atrial fibrillation. Chest. 2010;137(2):263-272.

spesi.title: sPESI score

items.label: Chronic cardiopulmonary disease (heart failure or chronic lung disease)

spesi.interpretation: A score of 0 identifies patients at low 30-day all-cause mortality risk and supports considering outpatient treatment or early discharge; any point (≥1) is "elevated risk" under the original derivation — this is a mortality-prognosis tool, not a direct substitute for a haemodynamic risk category. The 2026 multisociety PE guideline retains sPESI (Class 1, Level of Evidence B-R) for identifying low clinical-severity (category A/B) disease.

source.text: Jiménez D, Aujesky D, Moores L, et al. Simplification of the pulmonary embolism severity index for prognostication in patients with acute symptomatic pulmonary embolism. Arch Intern Med. 2010;170(15):1383-1389.

bova.title: Bova score

items.label: RV dysfunction on echocardiography or CT

bova.interpretation: Validated only in normotensive PE patients (systolic BP >90 mmHg at presentation). Stage I (0-2 points) = low, Stage II (3-4) = intermediate, Stage III (>4) = high 30-day risk of PE-related complications (death, haemodynamic collapse, or recurrent PE needing escalation) — not all-cause mortality, and not equivalent to simply having both RV dysfunction and an elevated troponin, since the two conditions are scored and weighted differently. The 2026 multisociety PE guideline lists a Bova score ≤4 among the criteria defining low clinical-severity (category C) disease.

source.text: Bova C, Sanchez O, Prandoni P, Lankeit M, Konstantinides S, Vanni S, Jiménez D. Identification of intermediate-risk patients with acute symptomatic pulmonary embolism. Eur Respir J. 2014;44(3):694-703.
